issues.description: Field Lecture.lectureName: the problem statement (UML and attribute list) and the template imply lectureName is a String, but the solution declares the field as type LectureName and provides a constructor parameter of type LectureName. The solution also includes a separate LectureName class. This mismatch between expected String and solution's LectureName type causes signature and assignment incompatibilities (e.g., the solution's getter and setter use String in their signatures but the field is LectureName), leading to compilation errors and preventing students from using the solution as a reference or tests that expect String-based APIs.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the type of lectureName consistent across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to use String for the lectureName field, constructor parameter, and corresponding getter/setter (remove the LectureName class). Update the solution constructor signature to public Lecture(String lectureName, int numberOfInscribedStudents, int numberOfGuestStudents, int numberOfLecturers, int numberOfTutors), update the field to private String lectureName, and ensure getLectureName()/setLectureName(...) use String. Alternatively, if the intention is to introduce a LectureName value object, update the problem statement, UML, and template to require LectureName consistently and change all method signatures and tests to use LectureName so all artifacts match.

issues.description: Concept: the lecture's name. Problem statement / UML: declares an attribute lectureName of type String (UML listing in problem_statement.md). Template: instructions/TODOs expect students to add an attribute lectureName as a String in src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java. Solution: introduces a wrapper type LectureName and declares the field as private LectureName lectureName and a constructor parameter LectureName lectureName (src/de/tum/cit/ase/Lecture.java) and provides a separate LectureName class (src/de/tum/cit/ase/LectureName.java). This mismatch (String vs LectureName) means students reading the UML/template will expect to work with a String but the solution uses a different type and identifier, increasing cognitive load and making it unclear which type and API are authoritative.
issues.suggestedFix: Align the representation of lectureName across artifacts. Preferred fix: change the solution to use a plain String for the lectureName field and constructor parameter (remove the LectureName wrapper class and update field, constructor, getters, setters and toString to use String). Alternative: if the wrapper is intentional, update the problem statement UML and the template to introduce and document the LectureName type and change all signatures to use LectureName so students and tests are consistent.
